blockers.description: SIX open PRs cover overlapping work from divergent lineages. This branch is 23 commits behind its own PR base (origin/feature/phase-7-exec), and two functionalscript minor versions behind main (0.41.0 vs 0.43.0). PRs #39 and #40 cover Phases 8 and 9 from a DIFFERENT branch line, each carrying 25-26 commits this branch does not have. #41 (31 commits) applies todo/feedback.md and retires the file. #38 (24 commits) fixes three review findings on my own PR #32.
blockers.workaround: None. Every additional commit here widens a merge surface someone reconciles by hand. Code changes are deliberately HELD; only documentation was touched after this was discovered.

blockers.description: A real bug ships on this branch and this branch's own tests protect it. fjs/server/fjs_run/module.f.js:275 serializes results with String(outcome.value). The guest ABI is Report<T> with T unconstrained, so a structured result becomes '[object Object]', which is then hashed, stored, and attested by the run record's resultHash. PR #38 already fixes it properly (withResultText).
blockers.workaround: Do NOT fix it here — #38's fix is better and a third implementation would conflict. Note the trap: the mutation sweep tested String -> JSON.stringify, saw 3 tests fail, and recorded it CAUGHT. The proofs use fixtures returning JSON strings, so stringify double-encodes and breaks them. The tests pin the bug. A red mutation means tests and code AGREE, not that the code is right.

decisions.decision: Zero observed CAS reads is an error result
decisions.rationale: PROV-07's kill condition for () => pure({ line16: 9137 }). Not a literal-count heuristic — a report that read nothing computed nothing. Accepted risk recorded in 09-CONTEXT.md: it rejects any program that legitimately computes without reading. None exists in scope.

decisions.decision: The literal audit is REPORTED, never refused
decisions.rationale: Every real program contains a zero or an index. Criterion 3 asks for visibility; criterion 4's failure is the perturbation gate's separate job.

decisions.decision: The guard lives in fjs/report/guard, not inside fjs/server/fjs_run
decisions.rationale: User-directed. Its only dependency is the Read type. The defect this phase shipped was a DUPLICATION, and a guard in its own module makes a second copy conspicuous — you would have to import it and then not use it.

decisions.decision: Bracket assertions cite Rev. Proc. 2024-40 read from the PDF, not 08-RESEARCH.md
decisions.rationale: Asserting against our own research notes only catches drift between research and code. Reading the governing document also catches an error in the research.

context_notes: The single most valuable thing to carry forward: this project shipped the same defect FOUR times — a proof whose expected side was not independent of the code under test — and every time the suite was fully green. A systematic mutation sweep (95 mutations, isolated /tmp copies) found 24 more; all are now closed. The rule and the technique are in AGENTS.md, because the same lesson had already been written into phase CONTEXT files and module docstrings and did not prevent a single recurrence. Two mechanical traps the sweep itself surfaced are documented there too: a repo copy shares the real .git (a commit from inside one is destructive), and once a proof hand-types an expected value that literal exists twice, so a careless sed mutates both and confirms nothing. What the sweep found is also worth carrying: the security-shaped code held under attack; the gaps were all in data-shaping code that ships real financial values.
